elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits termination "by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other", and the notice "shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated", so the Company holds a without-cause exit whose effective date it selects (the Company's side is untouched by the new HDI term-end limitation).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice period remains ninety (90) days; no 30-day Company notice was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic anywhere in the rendered language; on the contrary, Section 4.2(a) requires the Company to pay HDI a Termination Payment on its own termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Any termination by HDI under this Section 4.1 shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term", so no HDI convenience termination can take effect during the committed one-year term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band, and the notice-specifies-date language makes this a termination right rather than a pure non-renewal mechanic. (The deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' probe returns false only because the phrase 'for convenience' is absent; substantively the without-cause right exists.)

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) as amended: "... the balance of which shall be divided by two, but in no event more than three (3) months of fees payable under Section 3." The cap is unconditional and sits at, not above, the fallback threshold.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: New sentence expressly ties the effective date of any HDI termination under Section 4.1 to "the end of the then-current term", satisfying the requirement that term-end limitation be express rather than inferred from the auto-renewal mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1 requires "ninety (90) days written notice" from the terminating Party, including HDI.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the retained mutual 90-day notice supplies both notice elements, the inserted proviso caps the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3 fees, and the inserted sentence expressly makes any HDI termination under Section 4.1 effective only at the end of the then-current term.

Preferred level fails on two elements: notice remains 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — instead the Company pays a Termination Payment. If the drafter wanted preferred, it would need a 30-day Company notice and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period.

Minimal: only two targeted insertions (the fee cap proviso and the HDI term-end limitation). The Net Sales formula, the $800,000 deduction, the divide-by-two mechanic and the eight-instalment quarterly payment schedule are all retained; no unrelated words were deleted and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories) were added.

Preserves intent: the "Termination Date" definition, the auto-renewal cycle, the Net Sales measurement window and the instalment timing survive intact. The retained sentence allowing a terminating Party's notice to specify the termination date is harmonised rather than contradicted, because the new sentence limits only the effectiveness of an HDI termination.

Residual point to note in the cover comment (not a defect at fallback): the cap refers to "fees payable under Section 3" — confirm Section 3 states a recurring fee against which three months can be measured (rather than only a Net Sales-based compensation formula), otherwise the cap could be difficult to compute in practice.

Optional hardening if the counterparty resists: state expressly that the Company may terminate "for convenience, in whole or in part, effective on the date specified in its notice", to remove any argument that Section 4.1 is only a non-renewal mechanic.
